dedupe_keys.name: a global dataset of annual urban extents 1992 2020 from harmonized nighttime lights

description: The global nighttime-light urban-extent research team publishes annual maps of developed areas from 1992 to 2020. The resource uses harmonised nighttime-light observations to derive a global urban sequence map and separate annual extent layers. Figshare lists the GeoTIFFs directly, with public and free access under CC-BY-4.0. The inspected repository description establishes global coverage and annual timing but does not state the output cell size or projection. Those details should be checked before combining the maps with infrastructure geometry. A limitation is that light-based urban classification can miss weakly illuminated development or include brightly lit non-residential areas. The series could calibrate regional urban-growth simulations or reconstruct changing exposure around transport and utility networks. It complements the underlying harmonised light-intensity product with a classified land-extent interpretation. No numerical values or classification accuracy were independently tested.
